subject: Trading
title: Algorithmic Chain Reactions
description: A short lesson to help you apply Algorithmic Chain Reactions.

hook.text: Modern markets are run by algorithms trading thousands of times per second. When they panic, it happens at light speed.

buildup.text: Many algorithms use similar signals: price, volume, and momentum. When one sells, it triggers others to sell.

discovery.text: This creates chain reactions—cascading sell-offs where machines amplify each other's actions with no human oversight.

twist.text: Algorithms don't feel fear—they just execute rules. But their collective behavior mimics panic perfectly.

climax.text: Regulators struggle to keep up. Markets move in milliseconds; regulatory responses take months or years.

punchline.text: When robots all run for the exit at once, the door is too small.

quiz.question: Why do algorithms create chain reactions?
options: Many use similar signals, so one selling triggers others to sell
Regulators program them to do so
